Gates fail: kelvin_ok=false (cable 1, both /SENSEC1_HI and /SENSEC1_LO unrouted — symmetric failure, kelvin_unrouted=1 confirmed), DRC=34, unconnected=3. Verdict is repair.

Critical observation: unconnected=3 but only 2 are accounted for by cable-1 Kelvin (kelvin_unrouted=1 → 2 ratlines). The directed stub summary shows all 7 stubs were absorbed or trimmed (absorbed=6 + trimmed_spurs=1 = n_stubs=7), meaning /CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, /I2C_SDA are fully connected — they contribute 0 to unconnected=3. The third unconnected ratline therefore belongs to a net that is (a) not a Kelvin net, (b) not in the compiler's stub injection list, and (c) not being targeted by any of the 81 standing rules. This is a coverage gap: when unconnected exceeds the sum of Kelvin-attributed ratlines (2×kelvin_unrouted + asymmetric Kelvin count), the residual excess is invisible to all current interventions.

Existing rules comprehensively cover the cable-1 symmetric Kelvin failure (Rules 33/34 force stubs, 55 failing_reasons extension, 56/57/58/59/60 corridor keepout escalation and ripup) and the Rule 46 co-fire with Rule 64's single-cable R+2 deferral. No new scorer metric improves on the existing 1000/unit for unconnected and kelvin_unrouted; raising either further does not differentiate candidates when all have the same Kelvin count. The DRC=34 at 200/unit (contributing 6800) is already dominant. No penalty raise is the right lever here.

The one genuinely new finding is the excess non-Kelvin unconnected ratline that has no targeted stub intervention. Manager rule targets this gap.
manager_rule: Maintain a session-scoped set 'compiler_excess_unconnected_targets' initialized to empty. After each round R: compute excess_unconnected = unconnected - (2 * kelvin_unrouted) - (count of cables C where exactly one of /SENSEC{C}_HI or /SENSEC{C}_LO appears in failing_reasons with 'has unconnected ratlines'). If excess_unconnected > 0: inspect the board to enumerate all nets with one or more unconnected ratlines; subtract from that set all Kelvin nets (/SENSEC{C}_HI and /SENSEC{C}_LO for all cable indices C) and all nets already in the compiler's current stub injection target list (i.e., nets that appeared in the directed stub summary 'nets' field in round R, regardless of absorbed/trimmed outcome); add each remaining net to compiler_excess_unconnected_targets; in round R+1, inject directed stubs for every net in compiler_excess_unconnected_targets using the same waypoint-compilation semantics as the existing /CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, /I2C_SDA mechanism. Remove a net from compiler_excess_unconnected_targets as soon as it no longer has unconnected ratlines (i.e., it does not contribute to excess_unconnected in any subsequent round). Do NOT add Kelvin nets to this set under any condition — those are governed by Rules 33/34/55. Log 'excess_non_kelvin_unconnected_stub_injection' with: (a) round R, (b) excess_unconnected count, (c) net names added to or retained in compiler_excess_unconnected_targets with their ratline counts, (d) nets removed from the set this round because they cleared, (e) kelvin_unrouted and unconnected values from round R. Rationale: round 116 has unconnected=3 with kelvin_unrouted=1 (2 Kelvin ratlines) and all 7 compiler stubs absorbed/trimmed (those 3 nets are connected), leaving exactly 1 unconnected ratline belonging to a net outside both the Kelvin set and the compiler's injection list. No existing rule detects or targets this residual. This rule closes that coverage gap by making the manager inspect and explicitly stub any non-Kelvin net that FR persistently fails to connect on its own.
